issues.legal_issue: The cost of plant and machinery situated in or upon land or a building is excluded when determining the rateable value for municipal property tax.
material_facts: The appeals challenged municipal property-tax assessments that included the cost of plant and machinery installed in or upon the assessed properties.

The disputed items included lifts and air-conditioning machinery; a notice purporting to treat lifts as part of buildings had been issued, but the court held the power under which it was issued invalid.
issues.conclusion: The cost of plant and machinery, including the lifts and air-conditioners in question, could not be included in the rateable value of the land or building.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 116(1) and 116(3) of the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957, the general rule is that plant and machinery is not counted in determining rateable value; the statutory exception depended on a valid notification, but Section 116(3) was invalid for excessive delegation. The court applied the distinction between land and buildings discussed in Poona Municipal Corporation v. Shankar Ramakrishna Jabade, and relied on Hindustan Lever Ltd. v. Municipal Corporation of Greater Bombay and New Manek Chowk Spg. and Wvg. Mills Co. Ltd. It also referred to the rateable-value principles in Patel Gordhandas Hargovindas v. Municipal Commissioner, Ahmedabad, and noted that the relevant 1994 bye-law provisions had been struck down, with that result left undisturbed in MCD v. Delhi Urban House Owner's Welfare Association.

predicates.municipal_property_tax_assessment_appeal: An assessed property owner or taxing authority challenged a municipal property-tax assessment in an appeal.
predicates.assessed_item_is_plant_or_machinery: The assessment included the cost of plant or machinery situated in or upon the land or building.

issues.definition: When a municipal property-tax assessment appeal concerns plant or machinery included in the assessment, its cost is excluded from rateable value.
